veranderings.rede: In Afrikaans water or an obstacle 'versper' someone's way; 'pad gestop' reads as a literal translation.
The second verb shares the subject 'Mense', so this is one sentence and AWS 2017 puts no comma before 'of'.

veranderings.voor: teen die seil en die skip beweeg
veranderings.na: teen die seil, en die skip beweeg
veranderings.rede: 'en' joins two sentences with their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma before it.
'vat' is colloquial here; 'beweeg' says the same thing in standard written Afrikaans without echoing 'trek'.

veranderings.voor: lang reise oor die oop see gevaar
veranderings.na: lang reise oor die oop see aangepak
veranderings.rede: One does not 'vaar' a journey in Afrikaans, and 'gevaar' here can be misread as the noun 'danger'; 'reise aanpak' is idiomatic and grade-appropriate.

veranderings.voor: van boomstompe, bamboes of riet saamgebind
veranderings.na: van saamgebinde boomstompe, bamboes of riet
veranderings.rede: The trailing participle is awkward word order; the attributive form reads naturally and keeps the meaning.

veranderings.voor: aan 'n mas wat die wind vang
veranderings.na: wat aan 'n mas hang en die wind vang
veranderings.rede: As written, 'wat die wind vang' grammatically refers to the mast, not the sail; this matches the study text's own wording and fixes the reference.

vlae.teks: Hy dra vrag betroubaar, maar hy is stadig.
vlae.rede: 'dra vrag betroubaar' is wooden, but any natural rewording (e.g. 'veilig', 'goed', 'swaar vrag') risks changing what is claimed, so it is left for the reviewer or writer.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: seile wat dun latte styf hou
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: In the Chinese jonk glossary entry this relative clause is ambiguous in Afrikaans: it can be read as sails that hold thin laths taut, the reverse of the intended meaning ('Dun latte hou sy seile styf'). A person may want to reword it, e.g. 'met seile wat deur dun latte styf gehou word'.
